Theme

Body, health & movement

anus noun

also rectum, back passage, bum hole

classical

Cic. Fam. 9.22; Cels. 7.30 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 59, 369 (for “rectum”)

ānus, ānī m.

noun, second declension

the anus

Literally a ring. Not to be confused with anus, anūs f., an old woman, with a short first vowel. Traupman gives ānus for “rectum”; Lewis & Short gives it only as the opening, the fundament, which is what it means here.

Other words

  • pōdex, pōdicis m. — the anus, the backside

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Hor. Epod. 8.6; Juv. 2.12 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx sermōnis humilis: Hor. Epod., Juv.)

    A coarse word of satire and invective, perhaps from pēdō, fart (Lewis & Short).

  • cūlus, cūlī m. — arse, arsehole

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Catull. 23.19; 33.4; Mart. 3.98.1 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx obscēna: Catull., Mart.)

    The vulgar word, found in Catullus and Martial; it lives on in Italian and Spanish culo.

See also bottom, bowels, empty the bowels.

SourcesLewis & Short: anus · Lewis & Short: podex · Lewis & Short: culus
